hardware_raytraced_gi.problem: Dynamic diffuse interreflection (infinite bounces) that reacts to moving lights and geometry, without precomputed lightmaps. Solves the 'baked lighting cannot respond to a time-of-day cycle or a destroyed wall' problem.

implementation_variants.name: Lumen Hardware Ray Tracing with Surface Cache (Unreal Engine 5)
implementation_variants.description: Trace rays against the TLAS/BLAS but shade hits from a cached surface-lighting atlas instead of evaluating full material shading at the hit point. Epic exposes this as the default 'Ray Lighting Mode: Surface Cache' for best performance, with 'Hit Lighting for Reflections' as the higher-quality option.

implementation_variants.name: Screen-space / world-space radiance probes with temporal accumulation
implementation_variants.description: Place probes in screen space (or a world-space probe volume), trace a small number of rays per probe, and accumulate radiance over many frames. Lumen's Final Gather is this family; the method is what makes GI affordable per-pixel.

implementation_variants.name: Screen-space ray-traced GI (SSGI) reusing the depth+colour buffer
implementation_variants.description: March the G-buffer depth in screen space to find one-bounce GI. Cheap, but cannot see off-screen geometry and leaks at screen edges.

implementation_variants.name: Cascaded / distance-field + heightfield fallback GI (software RT)
implementation_variants.description: When no hardware RT is available, Lumen falls back to tracing against per-mesh and global distance fields ('Software Ray Tracing Mode: Detail Tracing' vs 'Global Tracing').

hardware_raytraced_gi.applicability_conditions: Requires RT-capable hardware + RHI + OS if HW RT is used; otherwise requires 'Generate Mesh Distance Fields' (engine restart) for the software path. Best on scenes that tolerate a multi-second global-light propagation latency. Static lights are NOT supported when Lumen is enabled.
hardware_raytraced_gi.limitations: Epic documents 'significant scene update costs for scenes with more than 100,000 instances' for hardware RT. Mesh Distance Fields 'increases build times, memory usage and disk size of Static Meshes'. Lumen only stores one depth layer, so light leaking can occur. Global changes (e.g. disabling the Sun) 'can take multiple seconds to propagate'. SW/HW RT is not a substitute for the raster G-buffer pass - it is an additional pass.
hardware_raytraced_gi.required_data_and_tools: Scene TLAS/BLAS (DXR: bottom-level + top-level acceleration structures) or prebuilt mesh distance fields; motion vectors and a stable G-buffer for temporal accumulation; a denoiser; GPU profiler with RT counters (Unreal Insights, Nsight Graphics).

hardware_raytraced_gi.quality_impact: Large: colour bleed, indirect shadowing and sky shadowing that baked lighting cannot express. Removes the baked/unlit look of dynamic objects in static scenes.
hardware_raytraced_gi.concept_impact: Enables fully dynamic time-of-day, destructible interior/exterior transitions and emissive-driven lighting. Removes the lightmap-bake iteration from the art loop.
hardware_raytraced_gi.recommended_stage: vertical_slice_or_later, once lighting art direction is locked; earlier only as a tech spike because surface-cache resolution knobs change the art look.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 15d RT/GI pass integration in an existing renderer + 10d probe/surface-cache plumbing + 10d denoise/temporal-stability + art re-tuning; assumes the engine already has a deferred/forward+ G-buffer and motion vectors

relations.note: Distance-field (software) tracing is Epic's documented fallback when hardware RT is unavailable.
Voxel cone tracing is an older, non-RT approach to the same one/two-bounce diffuse GI problem.
Baked lighting solves the same problem with zero runtime GI cost but no dynamic response.
Temporal accumulation of probe radiance is what makes the per-frame ray count affordable.
SSGI is a cheaper subset that is often combined with, rather than replacing, hardware RT GI.
Moving from cached-surface RT GI to full path tracing changes cost by an order of magnitude; CDPR gates it to top-tier GPUs and ships it off by default.

hardware_raytraced_gi.verification: Freeze the camera and record GPU ms for the RT-GI pass alone (not the whole frame). Turn the sun off and measure wall-clock seconds until the GI converges to the new solution. Count invalidated/updated instances against Epic's >100,000-instance warning. Verify on the minimum supported GPU, not the dev GPU.

sdf_global_illumination.problem: Dynamic GI on hardware without ray-tracing units, by tracing against a signed distance field representation instead of triangles.

implementation_variants.name: Per-mesh distance fields (Detail Tracing)
implementation_variants.description: Trace against each mesh's own distance field for the highest quality. Lumen exposes this as 'Software Ray Tracing Mode: Detail Tracing'.

implementation_variants.name: Global distance field (Global Tracing)
implementation_variants.description: Trace against a single merged, lower-detail global distance field - 'fastest traces' per Epic.

implementation_variants.name: Distance-field cone tracing for AO / occlusion
implementation_variants.description: Cone-march the distance field to get cheap, stable occlusion and short-range GI. Lumen states it 'replaces Distance Field Ambient Occlusion (DFAO)'.

implementation_variants.name: Global SDF for non-rendering systems (audio/wind/AI)
implementation_variants.description: The same SDF volume is reused for gameplay queries; Remedy's Alan Wake 2 wind system is built on 'Signed Distance Fields (SDF) methods where wind boxes are used as primitives'.

sdf_global_illumination.applicability_conditions: Requires generation of mesh distance fields at cook time and an engine restart in UE. Works on non-RT hardware. Requires static/near-static geometry for the field to stay valid; heavy WPO/skeletal deformation invalidates it.
sdf_global_illumination.limitations: Distance fields are a low-frequency proxy: thin geometry and small detail disappear, and 'Distance Field Voxel Density' with large values 'consume memory very quickly'. They cannot represent per-triangle material detail, so they are not a path-tracing substitute.
sdf_global_illumination.required_data_and_tools: Mesh distance field baker (UE 'Generate Mesh Distance Fields'), a voxel density budget, and a visualiser for the SDF (UE 'Distance Fields' view mode).

impact.gpu: medium (lower than HW RT GI on the same scene)
impact.vram: medium (SDF volume scales with voxel density and scene bounds)
impact.disk: medium (baked SDF data on Static Meshes)

sdf_global_illumination.quality_impact: Medium-high: real indirect bounce and sky shadowing, but softer and lower-frequency than triangle-accurate RT.
sdf_global_illumination.concept_impact: Lets a game ship dynamic GI on the installed base rather than only on RT GPUs. Enables a single lighting code path across console and low-end PC tiers.
sdf_global_illumination.recommended_stage: prototype_to_vertical_slice if the target hardware lacks RT; requires an up-front memory budget for the SDF volume.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 10d SDF generation/integration + 10d cone-trace GI pass + 10d tuning voxel density vs memory; assumes an engine that already has a GI slot to fill (e.g. UE Lumen)

relations.note: Same problem, different acceleration structure: SDF vs BVH/TLAS.
Both are volumetric approximations; SDF avoids the voxelisation step but carries less material information.
The same distance field serves both GI tracing and long-range shadows.
Nanite-style virtualised geometry changes the SDF generation path; Epic ties SDF generation specifically to Static Meshes.

sdf_global_illumination.verification: Visualise the SDF and compare a static lit scene against an offline path-traced reference; measure the VRAM of the SDF volume at the chosen 'Distance Field Voxel Density' and confirm it fits the min-spec budget; check thin-geometry leakage on hand-picked art.

screen_space_gi.problem: Cheap one-bounce indirect light using only the already-rendered depth and colour buffers, for games that cannot afford world-space GI.

implementation_variants.name: Screen Traces inside Lumen
implementation_variants.description: Epic exposes 'Screen Traces': 'Whether to use screen space traces for Lumen Global Illumination. Screen space traces bypass Lumen Scene and instead sample Scene Depth and Color.'

implementation_variants.name: Depth-buffer ray march with hierarchical acceleration (Hi-Z march)
implementation_variants.description: March the depth pyramid to find the first hit, then sample the previous frame's lit colour for the incoming radiance. Needs temporal accumulation to hide the missing off-screen data.

implementation_variants.name: Screen-space GI restricted to a half/quarter-res buffer, upscaled
implementation_variants.description: Run the march at reduced resolution and upscale - the same 'compute volumetrics/GI low, apply at full res' pattern Epic's VSM docs describe for coarse pages.

implementation_variants.name: SSR-style specular-only variant (cheapest)
implementation_variants.description: Limit the march to specular reflections, where missing information is less objectionable than in diffuse GI.

screen_space_gi.applicability_conditions: Any G-buffer renderer. Requires a jittered temporal upscaler or a temporal filter to be usable at all, because a single-frame screen-space result is noisy and unstable.
screen_space_gi.limitations: Fundamentally cannot see off-screen or occluded geometry. Epic notes that enabling screen traces 'prevents from Lumen Scene only changes, like adding emissive objects that are only visible in global illumination'. Screen-edge and disocclusion artefacts are inherent.
screen_space_gi.required_data_and_tools: Scene depth (Hi-Z/mip chain), previous-frame lit colour, motion vectors, a temporal accumulator, and a half/quarter-res render target.

impact.gpu: low to medium (scales with screen resolution and march step count)

screen_space_gi.quality_impact: Low-medium: adds contact-bounce colour bleed near visible surfaces; visibly wrong at screen edges and behind occluders.
screen_space_gi.concept_impact: High value per millisecond for stylised or indoor games; low value for open-world daylight.
screen_space_gi.recommended_stage: vertical_slice; cheap to add, so it can also be a late-game polish toggle behind a scalability tier.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 5d march + 4d temporal accumulation/rejection + 3d artefact tuning; assumes an existing depth pyramid and temporal upscaler

irradiance_volume_probes.problem: Give dynamic and static objects a plausible indirect-light response at near-zero runtime cost, including off-screen information that screen-space methods cannot see.

implementation_variants.name: Light probe groups / probe volumes baked at cook time
implementation_variants.description: Spherical-harmonic irradiance probes placed (manually or automatically) in the level and baked offline; runtime cost is a few texture fetches and an SH dot product.

implementation_variants.name: Probes re-lit at runtime on a slow schedule
implementation_variants.description: Re-trace a small number of rays per probe per frame into an atlas, spreading the cost over seconds - the same temporal-slicing idea as Lumen's caches.

implementation_variants.name: Volumetric/probe-based fog lighting
implementation_variants.description: The same probe volume is sampled by the volumetric fog pass, giving fog a light response that matches surfaces.

implementation_variants.name: Per-object / per-character interpolated probes
implementation_variants.description: Sample the nearest N probes and blend; used to keep characters lit consistently as they move between lighting zones.

irradiance_volume_probes.applicability_conditions: Works on any hardware, including mobile. Requires level authoring discipline (probe placement or auto-placement density) and lightmap UVs are not required.
irradiance_volume_probes.limitations: Low-frequency only: light leaking through thin walls and missing contact shadows. Probe interpolation artefacts on moving objects. Baking needs a rebuild when lighting changes.
irradiance_volume_probes.required_data_and_tools: Probe placement tooling (auto or manual), an SH bake (CPU or GPU), and a debug view that shows probe positions and interpolated values.

impact.cpu: low (bake only, unless re-lit at runtime)
impact.gpu: low
impact.vram: low (probe atlas; scales with probe count x SH coefficients)
impact.disk: low to medium (baked probe data per level)

irradiance_volume_probes.quality_impact: Medium: removes the 'floating in a void' look of unlit dynamic objects; does not give contact detail.
irradiance_volume_probes.concept_impact: Enables dynamic objects and characters in a baked world; the standard fallback when full dynamic GI is unaffordable.
irradiance_volume_probes.recommended_stage: prototype; probe density should be decided with level design, not bolted on late.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 6d probe placement/auto-placement tooling + 5d bake + 4d runtime sampling and leak fixing

relations.note: Lightmaps handle static surfaces, probes handle dynamic objects - the classic shipped pairing.
Dynamic GI removes the bake but costs far more GPU.
SSGI gives higher-frequency detail but no off-screen data.
Both are spatial caches of irradiance; a radiance cache is the dynamic, temporal version.

temporal_radiance_cache.problem: Amortise the cost of dynamic GI by storing radiance in a cache and only re-tracing a fraction of it each frame, so GI is affordable without a full per-pixel trace every frame.

implementation_variants.name: Screen-space radiance cache / Final Gather with temporal accumulation
implementation_variants.description: Lumen's Final Gather accumulates radiance over time; quality is traded against convergence speed with 'Lumen Scene Lighting Update Speed' and 'Final Gather Lighting Update Speed'.

implementation_variants.name: World-space irradiance/radiance cache (cascaded or probe-based)
implementation_variants.description: Persist radiance in world space so it survives camera cuts and can be re-used by any viewer; the classic alternative to screen-space caching.

implementation_variants.name: Shared ray-trace buffer reused by multiple effects
implementation_variants.description: Trace once, consume many times. Metro Exodus 'Added buffer to cache raytrace data for use in RTAO and RTGI passes - Why do it 1000 times when once will do?'

implementation_variants.name: History resurrection / persistent frame history
implementation_variants.description: UE's TSR 'History Resurrection' 'recalls stored data from past frames when they show up again in the current frame'; the same idea applies to a radiance cache so that re-appearing geometry does not have to re-converge.

temporal_radiance_cache.applicability_conditions: Requires stable world-space or screen-space parameterisation, correct motion vectors, and content that does not change lighting abruptly every frame.
temporal_radiance_cache.limitations: Latency: Epic states global changes 'can take multiple seconds to propagate'. Raising update speed costs GPU directly ('Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost'). Cache misses after camera cuts show as a visible converge-in.
temporal_radiance_cache.required_data_and_tools: A cache data structure (screen-space or world-space atlas), motion vectors, an invalidation heuristic, and a GPU profiler that can isolate the cache update pass.

impact.gpu: medium

temporal_radiance_cache.quality_impact: Medium-high: makes dynamic GI affordable; quality is bounded by the convergence latency, not by the ray count.
temporal_radiance_cache.concept_impact: The enabling technique for dynamic GI on consoles; without it, per-pixel dynamic GI is not shippable at 60 FPS.
temporal_radiance_cache.recommended_stage: vertical_slice; the cache is part of the GI system, not a post-hoc optimisation.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 12d cache data structure + 8d invalidation/temporal rejection + 8d latency tuning against art-direction sign-off

Update speed is a natural scalability knob.

voxel_cone_tracing.problem: Real-time diffuse (and glossy) indirect illumination without hardware ray tracing, by voxelising the scene and cone-marching a mip-mapped voxel representation.

implementation_variants.name: Sparse voxel octree (SVO) cone tracing - the original Crassin et al. formulation
implementation_variants.description: Voxelise the scene into a hierarchical voxel octree on the fly, inject direct lighting, then cone-trace the mip hierarchy for diffuse and glossy GI and for AO.

implementation_variants.name: Clipmap / cascaded voxel grid instead of an SVO
implementation_variants.description: Use a fixed set of nested 3D textures (clipmaps) around the camera rather than a sparse octree - simpler, constant memory, coarser far field.

implementation_variants.name: Voxelised volume reused for volumetrics and fog
implementation_variants.description: The same voxel volume feeds volumetric scattering, which is how several shipped engines justified the voxelisation cost.

implementation_variants.name: Sparse/partial re-voxelisation of dynamic objects only
implementation_variants.description: Re-voxelise only moving objects each frame and keep static geometry in the volume, cutting the per-frame voxelisation cost.

voxel_cone_tracing.applicability_conditions: Works on non-RT hardware (compute-capable GPU). Requires a voxelisation pass and memory for the volume. Best for indoor/medium-scale scenes where the voxel grid resolution is adequate.
voxel_cone_tracing.limitations: Voxelisation is a per-frame cost and a memory cost; thin geometry leaks; light leaks through walls at coarse mips. The published framerate (25-70 FPS) is from 2011 hardware and the authors' scenes. Large open worlds need clipmapping, which adds complexity.
voxel_cone_tracing.required_data_and_tools: A voxelisation compute/graphics pass, a 3D texture or SVO with mips, conservative rasterisation or a compute voxeliser, and a volume visualiser.

impact.gpu: medium to high (voxelisation + cone tracing)

voxel_cone_tracing.quality_impact: Medium: soft, plausible GI and cheap AO; lower fidelity than triangle-accurate RT and prone to light leaking.
voxel_cone_tracing.concept_impact: Historically important; largely superseded in shipping engines by distance-field and hardware-RT approaches, but still a valid non-RT option.
voxel_cone_tracing.recommended_stage: prototype_only unless the target platform forbids both RT and SDF tracing; the engineering cost is high relative to modern alternatives.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 20d voxelisation + 20d cone-trace + 15d leak/artefact tuning and dynamic-object path; high because there is no off-the-shelf engine path in UE/Unity today

implementation_variants.name: Tiled / clustered light list with a per-tile light cap
implementation_variants.description: Assign lights to screen tiles or view-space clusters and cap the list length per tile. Olsson et al. measured clustered light assignment at 0.71 ms for 32 lights and 1.42 ms for 32,768 lights, versus 0.24 ms and 9.31 ms for tiled.

dynamic_light_priority_budget.applicability_conditions: Requires a forward+ or deferred renderer that can bind a per-tile/cluster light list. Doom Eternal shows it works in a fully forward renderer too.
dynamic_light_priority_budget.limitations: Caps cause popping when a light enters/leaves the list unless hysteresis or fading is added. Very large numbers of lights still cost shading time even with perfect culling.
dynamic_light_priority_budget.required_data_and_tools: A light list builder (compute), a tile/cluster resolution choice, GPU profiling of the binning pass in isolation, and a debug view of lights-per-pixel.

impact.gpu: medium

dynamic_light_priority_budget.quality_impact: Neutral if the budget is generous; visible light popping if it is not.
dynamic_light_priority_budget.concept_impact: Enables thousands of small lights (projectiles, impact decals, enemy light rigs) as a gameplay/art vocabulary.
dynamic_light_priority_budget.recommended_stage: vertical_slice; the light budget must be set before content is authored at scale.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 8d list builder + 5d caps/priority policy + 5d popping/hysteresis tuning

light_range_attenuation_lod.applicability_conditions: Any renderer with per-light cost. Needs a fade mechanism to avoid popping, and art sign-off on where the LOD boundary sits.
light_range_attenuation_lod.limitations: Risk of visible 'light popping' or a brightness step as the player crosses a threshold. Must be tuned per content type (a dim corridor light behaves differently from a searchlight).
light_range_attenuation_lod.required_data_and_tools: A per-light LOD parameter in the light component, a distance metric, and a screenshot-diff test to catch brightness steps.

impact.gpu: low to medium

light_range_attenuation_lod.quality_impact: Low if faded correctly; a brightness or shadow 'pop' is otherwise very visible.
light_range_attenuation_lod.concept_impact: Lets designers place many more lights than the raw budget allows, at the cost of a distance-dependent look.
light_range_attenuation_lod.recommended_stage: production; it is a tuning pass that needs representative content.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 3d LOD parameter + 3d fade implementation + 2d per-content tuning

cascaded_shadow_maps.problem: Give a directional (sun/moon) light shadow coverage over a large view distance without the texel-density collapse of a single shadow map.

implementation_variants.name: Classic cascaded shadow maps with per-cascade matrices and a cascade blend band
implementation_variants.description: Split the view frustum along depth into N cascades, render one shadow map per cascade, and blend at the boundaries to hide the resolution step.

implementation_variants.name: Cascades generated by a virtualised/clipmapped system (UE5 Virtual Shadow Maps)
implementation_variants.description: UE5 replaces hand-tuned CSM with clipmaps: 'Directional Lights use a clipmap structure of expanding ranges around the camera, with each clipmap level having its own 16K VSM.', default levels 6-22 (64 cm to ~40 km).

implementation_variants.name: Cascade count and distance as a scalability knob
implementation_variants.description: Reduce cascade count / shorten the shadow distance on low tiers; UE keeps 'Dynamic Shadow Distance Movable Light' as the hand-off point to distance-field shadows.

implementation_variants.name: Cached static cascades re-rendered only when the light or geometry moves
implementation_variants.description: Separate static from dynamic casters so the static cascade is rendered once. Epic's VSM does this with 'Separate Static Caching'.

cascaded_shadow_maps.applicability_conditions: Any renderer. Cost is dominated by the geometry rendered into each cascade, so it favours engines with good LODs or virtualised geometry.
cascaded_shadow_maps.limitations: Aliasing and peter-panning at grazing sun angles; cascade seams; a sun that moves forces a full re-render every frame. UE documents that VSM 'greatly increase[s] resolution, but shallow light angles / projective aliasing ... can exhaust available virtual resolution'.
cascaded_shadow_maps.required_data_and_tools: A shadow-caster culling path, cascade split parameterisation (logarithmic vs practical), a shadow-depth render pass, and a debug view of cascade colours.

impact.gpu: medium

cascaded_shadow_maps.quality_impact: High: shadow coverage is the single biggest readability cue in outdoor scenes.
cascaded_shadow_maps.concept_impact: Standard requirement for any outdoor directional-light game.
cascaded_shadow_maps.recommended_stage: prototype; nearly every engine ships something here, so the decision is how many cascades and how far, not whether.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 6d cascade setup + 4d seam/bias tuning + 4d caster culling and cost control

virtual_shadow_maps.problem: Very high resolution, stable shadows for many lights without the VRAM cost of large conventional shadow maps, by virtualising the shadow map into pages that are allocated and cached only where needed.

implementation_variants.name: Unreal Engine 5 Virtual Shadow Maps (16k x 16k pages of 128x128)
implementation_variants.description: 'VSMs split the shadow map into tiles (or Pages) that are 128x128 each. Pages are allocated and rendered only as needed to shade on-screen pixels based on an analysis of the depth buffer.' Directional lights use clipmaps (default levels 6-22), spots a 16k VSM with mips, points a cube of six 16k faces.

implementation_variants.name: Virtual shadow maps with static/dynamic page separation
implementation_variants.description: 'VSM stores effectively two copies of depth: static and dynamic ... when the dynamic geometry moves, there is no need to redraw the static geometry.' The target is 'invalidated' static pages 'near 0'.

implementation_variants.name: Shadow Map Ray Tracing (SMRT) for soft penumbrae
implementation_variants.description: Filter by tracing rays through the virtual pages rather than by PCF taps: 'r.Shadow.Virtual.SMRT.RayCountLocal' / 'RayCountDirectional' default to 8 rays at Epic scalability; 'Using values between 4 and 8 samples works well' for samples-per-ray.

implementation_variants.name: Coarse pages for non-screen-space consumers (volumetric fog, forward translucency)
implementation_variants.description: 'Coarse Pages' are marked for systems that sample shadows at arbitrary locations such as Volumetric Fog; they 'Can hurt performance, especially with non-Nanite dynamic geometry due to draw-call bottlenecks.'

virtual_shadow_maps.applicability_conditions: Epic states VSMs 'are currently targeted at high-end desktops and next-generation consoles'. Requires virtualised geometry (Nanite) or complete mesh LOD chains to be cheap, because 'Non-Nanite geometry is much more expensive to render into VSMs than Nanite geometry'.
virtual_shadow_maps.limitations: Single physical page pool: 'If the number of Pages exceeds Max Pages corruption will occur, which sometimes manifests visually as a checkerboard pattern, or corrupt or missing shadows.' Many small local lights remain 'a work in progress'. Low-poly geometry shows the shadow-terminator problem. Only the first depth layer is stored, so overlapping occluders can leak and penumbrae can be inconsistent.
virtual_shadow_maps.required_data_and_tools: A page allocator and page-table build pass, a depth-buffer analysis pass, a physical page pool sized by 'r.Shadow.Virtual.MaxPhysicalPages', and 'r.Shadow.Virtual.Visualize' plus Unreal Insights ('trace.enable counters, vsm') for profiling.

impact.gpu: medium (two separable costs: Shadow Depths = pages x geometry; Shadow Projection = total shadow-map samples across the screen)
impact.vram: medium to high (single large physical page pool; overflow corrupts shadows)

virtual_shadow_maps.quality_impact: Very high: Epic notes the resolution is high enough that 'the Contact Shadow Length property is no longer necessary for sharp contact shadows'.
virtual_shadow_maps.concept_impact: Removes the hand-tuned cascade/inset/preshadow zoo; enables consistent shadow quality for large numbers of local lights.
virtual_shadow_maps.recommended_stage: vertical_slice_or_later on UE5 (it is the default); requires the project to commit to Nanite and tight object bounds.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 5d enabling/config on UE5 + 6d page-pool and resolution bias tuning + 5d invalidation hygiene (tight bounds, WPO disable distance) + 4d local-light cost control; NOT the cost of building a VSM system from scratch, which would be several times larger

Volumetric fog forces coarse pages, which Epic warns can hurt performance with non-Nanite dynamic geometry.

distance_field_shadows.problem: Long-range, stable soft shadows from a directional light where conventional shadow-map resolution collapses.

implementation_variants.name: Ray-marched distance-field shadows for directional lights
implementation_variants.description: Trace (march) the global/mesh distance field from the surface towards the light to compute a soft shadow; Epic recommends it 'beyond the Cascaded Shadow Maps property Dynamic Shadow Distance Movable Light'.

implementation_variants.name: Distance-field soft shadows as a scalability fallback
implementation_variants.description: Use cheap DFAO/DF shadows on low tiers where VSM or RT shadows are unaffordable.

implementation_variants.name: Distance fields reused by other systems to amortise their cost
implementation_variants.description: The same SDF volume powers GI tracing, AO and even gameplay queries (e.g. Remedy's SDF wind field in Alan Wake 2), which is how the memory cost is justified.

distance_field_shadows.applicability_conditions: Requires baked mesh distance fields (UE: 'Generate Mesh Distance Fields', engine restart). Works on non-RT hardware. Best for large-scale outdoor shadowing.
distance_field_shadows.limitations: Low frequency: fine contact detail is lost, and small/thin geometry may not appear. Memory scales with voxel density. Not supported for local lights in the same way - Epic notes 'selecting Distance Field shadows for them overrides the active shadow map method'.
distance_field_shadows.required_data_and_tools: Distance field baker, a voxel density budget, and a ray-march shadow pass.

impact.gpu: low to medium

distance_field_shadows.quality_impact: Medium: convincing large-scale shadowing, insufficient for contact detail.
distance_field_shadows.concept_impact: Lets a project extend the perceived shadow distance well past the CSM range.
distance_field_shadows.recommended_stage: production tuning; it is added once the base shadow system and its distance budget exist.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 3d enabling + 3d march/quality tuning + 4d memory/density budget work

screen_space_contact_shadows.problem: Small-scale contact darkening that no world-space shadow map can resolve at reasonable resolution.

implementation_variants.description: Short ray march in screen space to detect nearby occluders; the standard approach, with the usual screen-space information limits.

implementation_variants.description: Epic recommends Contact Shadows for grass and foliage 'when high-res shadows are not needed', and to use them instead of distant dynamic shadow casting.

implementation_variants.name: Screen-space AO-derivative contact darkening
implementation_variants.description: Derive contact darkening from the AO term rather than a separate march - cheapest, least accurate.

screen_space_contact_shadows.applicability_conditions: Any deferred/forward+ renderer with scene depth. Cheap enough for mid-tier hardware.
screen_space_contact_shadows.limitations: Inherently screen-space: no off-screen occluders, artefacts at screen edges, sensitivity to depth discontinuities, and instability under camera motion without temporal filtering.
screen_space_contact_shadows.required_data_and_tools: Scene depth (preferably a Hi-Z mip chain), previous-frame colour for temporal stabilisation, and a half-res buffer.

impact.gpu: low

screen_space_contact_shadows.quality_impact: Medium-high for grounding objects; purely additive to readability.
screen_space_contact_shadows.concept_impact: Lets designers get believable contact without raising the whole shadow-map budget.
screen_space_contact_shadows.recommended_stage: vertical_slice; cheap to add and to remove.

implementation_variants.name: Explicit occluder polygons with a per-light caster mask
implementation_variants.description: Only LightOccluder2D nodes cast; 'Occluder Light Mask ... is used in tandem with PointLight2D and DirectionalLight2D's Shadow > Item Cull Mask property to control which objects cast shadows for each light. This can be used to prevent specific objects from casting shadows.'

implementation_variants.name: Distance culling of casters (Max Distance in pixels)
implementation_variants.description: 'Max Distance: The maximum distance from the camera center objects can be before their shadows are culled (in pixels). Decreasing this value can prevent objects located outside the camera from casting shadows (while also improving performance).'

implementation_variants.name: Shadow filter LOD (None / PCF5 / PCF13 ladder)
implementation_variants.description: 'The default None is the fastest to render ... If you want a soft shadow, use PCF5 instead. PCF13 is even softer, but is the most demanding to render. PCF13 should only be used for a few lights at once due to its high rendering cost.'

implementation_variants.description: 'Additive sprites are much faster to render, since they don't need to go through a separate rendering pipeline ... it may be worth replacing some of them with Sprite2D nodes that use additive blending.' Trade-off: 'Additive sprites cannot cast shadows, since they are not lights.'

shadow_caster_2d_limits.applicability_conditions: Any 2D engine with a light/occluder model; the specific knobs quoted are Godot 4.x.

static_shadow_caching.problem: Re-rendering shadows for geometry that did not move is pure waste; in a mostly-static scene this dominates the shadow cost.

implementation_variants.name: Separate static and dynamic shadow pages (UE5 VSM)
implementation_variants.description: 'VSM stores effectively two copies of depth: static and dynamic. Thus, when the dynamic geometry moves, there is no need to redraw the static geometry. Instead, the cached static page can be cheaply composited on top.' Target: invalidated static pages 'should be near 0'.

implementation_variants.name: Per-primitive invalidation behaviour (Auto / Always / Rigid / Static)

implementation_variants.name: Fully baked static shadows in lightmaps

static_shadow_caching.applicability_conditions: Requires the shadow system to be page- or tile-addressable so partial invalidation is possible. Needs artists to mark mobility correctly and to keep object bounds tight.
static_shadow_caching.limitations: Epic warns that when WPO is used 'the actual displacement is not known until the object is rendered ... the Virtual Shadow Map cache system has to assume the object needs to be redrawn'. Over-large bounds invalidate more of the map than necessary.
static_shadow_caching.required_data_and_tools: A cache-invalidation API on primitives, a visualisation of cached (green) / new-invalidated (red) / static-only (blue) pages, and Unreal Insights VSM counters.

lightmap_atlas_baking.problem: Get high-quality multi-bounce global illumination and soft area-light shadowing at essentially zero runtime cost by precomputing it into textures.

implementation_variants.name: Traditional lightmap atlas with per-object UV packing
implementation_variants.description: Pack unique UVs into atlases, bake irradiance offline, sample at runtime. Requires a dedicated lightmap UV channel and costs disk + VRAM per level.

implementation_variants.name: Baking as the default path, with Lumen explicitly disabling it
implementation_variants.description: 'When Lumen is enabled for a project, precomputed static lighting contributions are disabled and all lightmaps are hidden.' Projects must 'Force No Precomputed Lighting' and rebuild to actually remove the data.

implementation_variants.name: Baked indirect + dynamic direct (stationary lights)
implementation_variants.description: 'Stationary lights still use baked indirect diffuse from lightmaps, but direct lighting/shadows are dynamic.' A common hybrid that keeps bounce quality while allowing a day/night cycle on direct light.

implementation_variants.name: Baked lighting + probe volumes for dynamic objects
implementation_variants.description: The classic shipped combination: static surfaces get lightmaps, moving objects sample probes.

lightmap_atlas_baking.applicability_conditions: Requires static or stationary geometry with unique UVs and a bake step in the content pipeline. Works on any hardware. Incompatible with fully dynamic GI in the same scene (Epic disables lightmaps when Lumen is on).
lightmap_atlas_baking.limitations: Zero runtime dynamism: moving lights, destructible geometry and time-of-day cannot be baked. Bake time is a pipeline cost. VRAM/disk scale with atlas resolution and level count. I could not verify a Unity or Epic primary page for bake times this pass (see SRC-RND-035 / SRC-RND-038).
lightmap_atlas_baking.required_data_and_tools: Lightmap UV generation, a baker (CPU or GPU), an atlas packer, per-platform lightmap resolution settings, and a streaming/compression story for the atlases.

gpu_lightmap_baking.problem: Lightmap bake times gate art iteration; moving the bake from CPU to GPU cuts the feedback loop from hours to minutes.

implementation_variants.name: Distributed / farm-based CPU bake with incremental re-bake
implementation_variants.description: Keep the CPU path but bake only changed tiles/levels incrementally; the standard fallback when GPU memory limits the scene size that can be baked.

implementation_variants.name: Bake on GPU with CPU fallback for out-of-core scenes
implementation_variants.description: Hybrid: GPU bake when the scene fits in VRAM, CPU farm otherwise. Requires matching output to avoid visual differences between paths.

gpu_lightmap_baking.recommended_stage: production, once lightmap content exists to bake; low value during pre-production.

lightmap_compression_streaming.problem: Lightmaps are one of the largest disk and VRAM consumers in a baked game; without compression and streaming, open worlds cannot ship.

implementation_variants.name: Block-compressed lightmaps (BC6H/BC7 or platform equivalents) with per-platform quality
implementation_variants.description: Compress at cook time with the platform's HDR/LDR block format; the standard approach. Banding in smooth gradients is the main artefact.

implementation_variants.name: Stream lightmaps per level/streaming-cell with mip streaming
implementation_variants.description: Only resident cells keep their lightmaps in VRAM. This is the same virtual-texturing/mip-streaming machinery engines already have for albedo.

implementation_variants.name: Reduce lightmap resolution per platform as a scalability tier
implementation_variants.description: Cook lower-resolution lightmaps for low-memory tiers; UE exposes platform lightmap resolution and 'Force No Precomputed Lighting' to drop them entirely.

implementation_variants.name: Remove lightmap data entirely when switching to dynamic GI
implementation_variants.description: Epic warns projects must enable 'Force No Precomputed Lighting' and rebuild, otherwise 'lightmaps are kept in memory/disk' even though hidden.

lightmap_compression_streaming.applicability_conditions: Only relevant if the project uses baked lighting. Requires the engine's texture streaming system to also handle lightmaps.
lightmap_compression_streaming.limitations: Compression artefacts (banding) on smooth gradients; streaming introduces pop-in on fast traversal; per-platform cooks multiply build time.
lightmap_compression_streaming.required_data_and_tools: A cook-time compression step, a streaming system with lightmap awareness, and a memory-report that breaks out lightmap VRAM per cell.

froxel_volumetric_fog.problem: Unified, physically-plausible atmospheric scattering and volumetric fog that applies correctly to opaque AND multiple transparent layers, at a shippable cost.

implementation_variants.name: Frustum-aligned froxel grid with exponential depth slices (Wronski / AC4)
implementation_variants.description: 'we decided to use layout aligned with the camera frustum. We directly map frustum to cuboid using normalized device coordinates in width x height axis and for depth slices we use exponential depth distribution' concentrated near the camera. Stored in 3D textures written by compute shaders with UAVs.

implementation_variants.name: Decoupled compute passes (density/injection -> lighting -> integration -> apply)
implementation_variants.description: 'Key idea of our algorithm is to decouple and parallelize typical steps of raymarching algorithms and launch them separately. This way we achieve parallelism and possibility of swapping and adjusting every element of the algorithm separately.' Measured: 'Total cost was surprisingly small, around 1.1ms ... Most costly part was building density and lighting the volume, around 0.43ms. Remaining passes were all under 0.2ms.'

implementation_variants.name: Quadrilinear-filtered application at full resolution
implementation_variants.description: 'Final application of effect on screen is trivial in both deferred and forward - no special tricks, just a simple bilinear look-up from a 3D texture and a fused multiply-add operation ... compatible with any number of transparent objects layers.'

implementation_variants.name: Async-compute overlap for the whole volumetric pass
implementation_variants.description: 'possibility of computing this pass in parallel with regular scene rendering as soon as shadow-maps are ready - for example using asynchronous compute on AMD hardware'.

froxel_volumetric_fog.applicability_conditions: Requires compute shaders with 3D-texture UAV writes (DX11-class or better). Needs shadow maps to be ready before the lighting pass. Fits both deferred and forward renderers.
froxel_volumetric_fog.limitations: The froxel grid is low resolution by design, so the effect is soft and 'missing high frequency geometric details'. Frustum alignment is 'prone to temporal aliasing and flickering' (mitigated later with temporal reprojection and jitter). Density authored as analytic noise lacks artist control unless painted.
froxel_volumetric_fog.required_data_and_tools: 3D textures with UAV access, a compute-capable pipeline, shadow maps (or a probe volume) for in-scattering, and a volumetric debug view.

impact.gpu: low to medium (measured ~1.1 ms total in AC4; 1.6 ms at double resolution)

froxel_volumetric_fog.quality_impact: Very high: light shafts, height fog and consistent transmittance across transparent layers. This is one of the highest quality-per-millisecond effects available.
froxel_volumetric_fog.concept_impact: Enables 'atmosphere as a gameplay/art element' and makes transparents (particles, water, glass) sit in the same medium as opaques.
froxel_volumetric_fog.recommended_stage: vertical_slice; atmosphere is part of art direction, so it must exist when the look is signed off.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 8d froxel volume + 6d lighting/integration + 4d temporal reprojection + 4d artist controls

implementation_variants.description: The canonical form: compute the volume at low resolution and apply it per-pixel with a filtered fetch. 'The resolution of our volume textures may seem extremely low, but it is sufficient ... we use quadrilinear filtering on volumetric data, we are unable to see single texels'.

implementation_variants.name: Multiple transparency resolutions (Alan Wake 2 MBOIT)

implementation_variants.description: Epic documents 'r.MotionBlur.HalfResInput' and 'r.MotionBlur.HalfResGather' as defaults on PS5/Xbox Series X, giving '3x the motion blur GPU performance cost' improvement.

volumetric_half_resolution.applicability_conditions: Any effect whose signal is low-frequency relative to the pixel grid. Fails for effects with high-frequency detail (thin light shafts, sharp god-ray edges) unless jittered and temporally accumulated.
volumetric_half_resolution.limitations: Reduces high-frequency detail and can create edge artefacts; needs temporal jitter + reprojection to be acceptable. Wronski notes the effect 'is very soft and is missing high frequency geometric details'.
volumetric_half_resolution.required_data_and_tools: A downsample/upsample pair, a bilateral or depth-aware upsample (naive bilinear creates halos), and a jittered sample pattern.

impact.gpu: low (saves a large fraction of the effect's cost)

volumetric_half_resolution.quality_impact: Low to medium loss for a large cost saving; the correct default for volumetrics.
volumetric_half_resolution.concept_impact: Lets a project ship volumetrics on mid-tier hardware at all.
volumetric_half_resolution.recommended_stage: vertical_slice; should be designed in, not retrofitted.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 4d resolution plumbing + 3d depth-aware upsample + 3d jitter/temporal stabilisation

selective_ray_traced_effects.problem: Full path tracing is unaffordable; picking a small set of effects to ray trace while the rest of the frame stays raster gives most of the perceived benefit at a fraction of the cost.

implementation_variants.name: Per-effect opt-in (RT shadows only, or RT reflections only, or RT AO only)
implementation_variants.description: The standard shipped approach. In UE, 'Ray-traced shadows still take precedence over VSMs', i.e. effects are individually overridden rather than the whole pipeline switched.

implementation_variants.name: Trace once, share the result across effects (RTAO + RTGI)
implementation_variants.description: Metro Exodus: 'Added buffer to cache raytrace data for use in RTAO and RTGI passes - Why do it 1000 times when once will do?'

implementation_variants.name: Screen-space ray tracing with spatio-temporal denoising
implementation_variants.description: Metro's RTGI was 'Raytracing in screen space', with all accumulation and denoising in that space, using distance-weighted spatial + temporal components and 'Fetch heavy data only if weight is non-zero'.

implementation_variants.name: Hardware RT for reflections only, with the Surface Cache for lighting
implementation_variants.description: Lumen's default: 'By default, Lumen uses Surface Cache for best performance, but can be set to Hit Lighting for Reflections for higher quality.'

selective_ray_traced_effects.applicability_conditions: Requires RT-capable hardware/RHI/OS. Each chosen effect needs a denoiser; without denoising, low sample counts are unusable. DXR defines the required pipeline: two-level acceleration structures (BLAS/TLAS) plus ray generation / closest hit / any hit / miss / intersection / callable shaders, with hit groups being '{0 or 1 intersection shader, 0 or 1 any hit shader, 0 or 1 closest hit shader}'.
selective_ray_traced_effects.limitations: RT effects are an ADDITIONAL pass on top of the raster pass, not a replacement for rasterisation - cost must be budgeted as an extra, and the raster G-buffer/depth work is still paid. Each added effect adds its own AS traversal and denoise cost. DXR shader-table constraints apply (shader identifier 32 bytes; max shader record stride 4096 bytes in multiples of 32; local root signature footprint capped at 4064 bytes).
selective_ray_traced_effects.required_data_and_tools: DXR or Vulkan RT: bottom-level acceleration structures per geometry and a top-level AS of instances; a denoiser (spatial + temporal); a GPU profiler that isolates each RT pass.

impact.gpu: medium to high (one additional pass per effect)

selective_ray_traced_effects.quality_impact: High for the chosen effects (correct reflections, contact-accurate shadows, no screen-space disocclusion holes).
selective_ray_traced_effects.concept_impact: The pragmatic path to 'ray-traced' shipping titles; full path tracing is a separate, much larger commitment.
selective_ray_traced_effects.recommended_stage: vertical_slice_or_later; requires the base render to be complete so that the RT pass is genuinely additive.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 8d AS management + 8d first RT effect + 8d denoiser integration + 6d per-effect budget/quality tiers

rt_effect_resolution_budget.problem: Ray tracing cost scales with rays x resolution; running RT passes below display resolution and caching/reusing their results is what makes them shippable.

implementation_variants.description: Trace at reduced resolution and rely on the denoiser plus a depth-aware upsample. The same reduced-resolution discipline as volumetrics, but the denoiser does more of the work.

implementation_variants.description: Metro Exodus: 'Added buffer to cache raytrace data for use in RTAO and RTGI passes - Why do it 1000 times when once will do?' This is caching at effect level rather than resolution level.

Smaller values save GPU memory, at a cost in quality. Defaults to 0.5 if not overridden.'

rt_effect_resolution_budget.applicability_conditions: Requires the denoiser to be able to operate at the reduced resolution without destroying detail; requires motion vectors for temporal reuse. SER requires hardware/driver support.
rt_effect_resolution_budget.limitations: Reduced resolution loses thin geometry and contact detail; denoising adds latency and can smear fast motion. The Surface Cache trades memory for quality and is itself a memory budget line.
rt_effect_resolution_budget.required_data_and_tools: A resolution-independent RT dispatch, an upsample that respects depth/normal discontinuities, and a per-pass GPU timing split (trace vs denoise vs upscale).

impact.gpu: low to medium (saves a large fraction of the RT pass cost)
impact.vram: medium (cache/history buffers; Surface Cache default 0.5 scale)

rt_effect_resolution_budget.quality_impact: Medium cost in sharpness and thin-detail fidelity for a large cost saving.
rt_effect_resolution_budget.concept_impact: Without resolution and caching budgets, RT effects cannot ship on mid-tier GPUs at all.
rt_effect_resolution_budget.recommended_stage: production tuning; needs a representative scene and target GPU.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 6d resolution plumbing + 6d denoiser retuning at new resolution + 6d cache/reuse plumbing

full_path_tracing_pipeline.problem: Unify direct and indirect lighting, reflections, refractions and shadows into one physically-correct algorithm, eliminating the per-effect approximation zoo.

implementation_variants.name: Progressive offline/reference path tracer (Unreal Path Tracer)
implementation_variants.description: 'The Path Tracer is a progressive, hardware-accelerated rendering mode that mitigates the disadvantages of real-time features with physically correct and compromise-free global illumination ... does not share the same ray-tracing code that has been developed to work well for real-time rendering.' Intended for ground-truth comparison and production renders, not gameplay.

implementation_variants.name: Real-time fully path-traced game (Quake II RTX)
implementation_variants.description: 'Quake II RTX is a pure ray-traced game. That means all lighting, reflections, shadows and VFX are ray-traced, with no traditional effects or techniques utilized.' NVIDIA newsroom calls it 'the world's first game that is fully path-traced'.

implementation_variants.name: Path tracing shipped as an optional ultra preset in a raster game (Cyberpunk 2077 Overdrive)
implementation_variants.description: CDPR added a preset above 'RT Ultra' that 'includes path-traced rendering'. Off by default; recommended on RTX 40 (4070 Ti and up); RTX 3090 only at 1080p 30 fps; VRAM 8/10/12 GB for 1080p/1440p/2160p.

implementation_variants.name: Path-traced indirect lighting layered on a raster pipeline
implementation_variants.description: Alan Wake 2 offers 'Path Traced Indirect Lighting' together with DLSS Frame Generation and DLSS Ray Reconstruction - i.e. PT for the indirect term only, not the whole frame.

full_path_tracing_pipeline.applicability_conditions: Requires DXR-capable hardware (Epic: Windows 10 1809+, NVIDIA RTX or DXR driver-enabled GTX, DX12). Requires the art to be authored for it: Epic recommends 'keep the Base Color below 0.8 for all diffuse materials' because high albedo lengthens paths. Requires a strong temporal upscaler + denoiser to be interactive at all.
full_path_tracing_pipeline.limitations: Cost. The strongest available evidence is CDPR gating it to RTX 4070 Ti+ and shipping it off by default. Epic notes the Path Tracer 'works by having the renderer accumulate samples over time. This is ideal for static scenes and less so for dynamic scenes ... moving lights, animated skinned meshes, and visual effects ... appear as blurred, or streaking artifacts'. Ray tracing does NOT replace rasterisation: it is a separate pass with its own cost, and the two must never be double counted in one pass description.
full_path_tracing_pipeline.required_data_and_tools: DXR/Vulkan RT pipeline (BLAS/TLAS, ray generation/closest-hit/miss/any-hit shaders), a denoiser (Epic defaults to NNE Denoise on GPU; OptiX and OIDN available), spp/bounce controls, and Movie Render Queue for reference renders.

impact.cpu: low to medium (AS rebuild for dynamic content)
impact.gpu: very high
impact.vram: high (AS + denoiser history + PT scratch; CDPR requires 8/10/12 GB by resolution)

full_path_tracing_pipeline.quality_impact: Highest available: unbiased GI, correct refractions, no per-effect approximation seams.
full_path_tracing_pipeline.concept_impact: Radically simplifies lighting authoring (no bake, no per-effect tuning) but restricts the shipping hardware to the top of the installed base.
full_path_tracing_pipeline.recommended_stage: late_production_or_post_launch as an optional ultra mode; not a baseline for a game with a broad PC target.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 20d PT kernel + 15d material/asset compatibility pass (Epic documents many 'experimental' feature statuses) + 20d denoiser/spp/quality tuning + 15d hardware tiering and validation; excludes the cost of re-authoring content albedo

implementation_variants.description: Epic: 'r.PathTracing.SpatialDenoiser.Type' selects spatial (0, default) or temporal (1); 'r.PathTracing.Denoiser.Name' selects NNEDenoiser (default) or OIDN; 'r.PathTracing.TemporalDenoiser.Name' selects NFOR (default), NNEDenoiser or OptiX. NNE Denoise 'is based on the same network as Intel's Open Image Denoise but runs it on the GPU'.

implementation_variants.name: Split samples across spatial and temporal axes
implementation_variants.description: 'The total number of samples taken per pixel is the product of the spatial and temporal sample counts. Spreading the samples across both spatial and temporal can produce better results in some cases. For example, if you want to use 16 samples per pixel, you could apply 4 samples to spatial and 4 to temporal ... For stills, we recommend using all spatial samples (1 temporal) and for animations, we recommend using 1 spatial sample with many temporal samples with reference motion blur turned on.'

implementation_variants.name: Bounce compaction to bound path length
implementation_variants.description: 'r.PathTracing.CompactionDepth ... By default, this console variable is set to 6, which means after 6 bounces, the path tracer will treat remaining bounces with a loop.'

implementation_variants.name: Spatio-temporal denoiser with distance weighting (shipped RTGI)
implementation_variants.description: Metro Exodus denoiser: spatial + temporal components, 'Distance weight', 'Radius of denoising', and 'Fetch heavy data only if weight is non-zero' to control bandwidth.

path_tracing_sample_denoiser_budget.applicability_conditions: Requires a denoiser that matches the content (animation vs still) and hardware; OIDN 'runs on the CPU and is not designed for interactive denoising'. Requires correct motion vectors for temporal accumulation.
path_tracing_sample_denoiser_budget.limitations: Denoising smears detail and can introduce ghosting on dynamic content; low spp plus fast motion produces boiling. Epic explicitly warns dynamic scene elements 'appear as blurred, or streaking artifacts'.
path_tracing_sample_denoiser_budget.required_data_and_tools: A denoiser library (NNE/OIDN/OptiX or in-house), spp and bounce controls, and a noise metric (variance over a frozen camera) to compare settings objectively.

deferred_forward_plus_choice.problem: Choose the lighting architecture that determines how many lights, what material variety, and what bandwidth/compute balance the renderer can afford.

implementation_variants.name: Deferred (G-buffer) shading
implementation_variants.description: One geometry pass, then screen-space lighting. Olsson et al. measured 'Deferred takes a total of 97.1 ms' on their test scene, showing the classic bandwidth/compute bound of naive deferred.

implementation_variants.name: Tiled / clustered deferred
implementation_variants.description: Adds a light list per tile or view-space cluster. Measured: 'The scene contains around 2400 light sources, and is rendered in 17ms by our method (2.3ms for clustering, 1.5ms for light assignment and 5.6 ms for shading)'.

implementation_variants.name: Forward+ (tiled/clustered forward)
implementation_variants.description: No G-buffer: cull lights per tile and shade in one forward pass, keeping MSAA and per-material shaders. Measured as very competitive: 'ClusteredForward offers very competitive performance, similar to TiledDeferred'; plain 'TiledForward 23.6 ms' on the same scene.

implementation_variants.name: Fully forward with hybrid cluster+tile binning (Doom Eternal / idTech 7)
implementation_variants.description: 'IDTECH 7 - Fully forward rendered - Still few uber shaders variations everything ... Still 60FPS on consoles at same resolutions.' Binning is a 'New hybrid of cluster and tile binning' with a 'Very tight budget (<500us)'.

deferred_forward_plus_choice.applicability_conditions: Deferred favours many lights + uniform materials; forward+ favours MSAA, varied materials and transparency. The clustered variants win once light counts pass roughly 2k: 'the crossover point between tiled and clustered implementations is at most around 2 k lights'.
deferred_forward_plus_choice.limitations: Deferred: G-buffer bandwidth and a fixed material model. Forward+: overdraw and per-material shader permutations. All screen-space variants: measured times (17 ms, 23.6 ms, 97.1 ms) are from a 2012 research implementation on 2012 hardware and must not be read as modern absolute numbers.
deferred_forward_plus_choice.required_data_and_tools: A G-buffer layout plan (deferred) or a light-list build pass (forward+), plus a GPU profiler that separates binning, assignment and shading.

impact.gpu: high (this is the single biggest architectural GPU decision after resolution)
impact.vram: high for deferred (G-buffer), lower for forward+

deferred_forward_plus_choice.quality_impact: Indirect: MSAA support, transparency correctness and material variety all follow from this choice.
deferred_forward_plus_choice.concept_impact: Determines the whole feature budget; changing it late is one of the most expensive changes in a rendering codebase.
deferred_forward_plus_choice.recommended_stage: pre_production; this must be decided before the renderer is built.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 15d G-buffer or light-list core + 12d material/lighting path + 10d MSAA/transparency handling + 8d validation; this is an architectural cost, not a feature cost

relations.note: Clustering is the technique that makes both deferred and forward+ scale to many lights.
A depth prepass reduces forward overdraw, which is forward+'s main weakness.
Light budgets are expressed through whichever architecture is chosen.
Uber-shader/bindless material models interact strongly with G-buffer packing and permutations.

deferred_forward_plus_choice.verification: Comparative test of both architectures on a reference scene at the target light count.

depth_prepass_early_z.problem: Overdraw: fragments shaded and then discarded because they are occluded. A cheap depth-only pass first lets the hardware reject them.

implementation_variants.name: Explicit depth-only prepass then a full material pass with depth test EQUAL
implementation_variants.description: The classic form; converts a shading-overdraw problem into a cheap depth-writing problem.

implementation_variants.name: Depth prepass feeding downstream passes (VSM page marking, SSAO, volumetrics)
implementation_variants.description: In UE5, VSM pages are allocated 'based on an analysis of the depth buffer', so the depth pass is not only an optimisation but a data dependency for shadows.

implementation_variants.name: Prepass used for GPU occlusion / meshlet culling in a GPU-driven pipeline
implementation_variants.description: Alan Wake 2 uses a GPU-driven pipeline with mesh shaders that achieves 'occlusion culling down to a single-pixel precision and use everything in a scene as an occluder', which replaces/augments a naive prepass.

implementation_variants.name: Front-to-back sorting as a cheaper alternative
implementation_variants.description: Sorting opaque draws front-to-back gets much of the early-Z benefit without a second geometry pass; effective when the geometry pass is not bandwidth-bound.

depth_prepass_early_z.applicability_conditions: Wins when the material shader is expensive relative to depth-only rasterisation, i.e. heavy PBR, hair, or many per-pixel lights. Loses when the scene is vertex-bound or draw-call-bound and geometry is cheap.
depth_prepass_early_z.limitations: Adds a full geometry pass (vertex cost) on scenes where the win is small. Requires a stable depth-prepass material (alpha-tested and WPO materials must match the main pass).
depth_prepass_early_z.required_data_and_tools: A depth-only pass with matching vertex shaders, an overdraw visualisation (shader complexity / overdraw view mode), and GPU timing split between prepass and main pass.

impact.gpu: low to medium (net win depends on overdraw factor)

depth_prepass_early_z.concept_impact: Enables expensive materials in dense scenes; also unlocks screen-space effects that need depth early.
depth_prepass_early_z.recommended_stage: vertical_slice; measure before committing, since it can be a net loss.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 4d prepass + 2d matching WPO/alpha-test path + 3d A/B measurement on representative scenes

dynamic_resolution_scaling.problem: Hold a frame-rate target on hardware whose cost varies with scene content, by scaling render resolution instead of dropping frames.

implementation_variants.name: GPU-timing heuristic with cruising inside a clamped range
implementation_variants.description: 'Dynamic Resolution adjusts the primary screen percentage according to the previous frames' GPU workload.' Defaults: 'r.DynamicRes.FrameTimeBudget' = 33.3 ms, 'MinScreenPercentage' = 50, 'MaxScreenPercentage' = 100.

implementation_variants.name: Over-budget 'panic' path
implementation_variants.description: Unpredictable spikes (camera cuts, expensive VFX) are handled by a fast drop: if the budget (33.3 ms) is exceeded for 'more than two frames consecutively', the heuristic resets its history and drops resolution immediately.

implementation_variants.name: Combined with a temporal upscaler (TSR/DLSS/FSR/XeSS)
implementation_variants.description: 'The renderer will now work with ResolutionFraction ... the upscale ratio is done by the TAA upsample or the spatial upscale ... 1 divided by the Resolution Fraction'. DRS and temporal upscaling are designed to be used together; Unreal warns 'r.DynamicRes.MinResolutionChangePeriod' exists partly to avoid 'Temporal Upsample's input sample offset interference'.

implementation_variants.name: CPU-bound screen percentage for shared-memory platforms
implementation_variants.description: 'r.DynamicRes.CPUBoundScreenPercentage' targets a primary screen percentage when CPU-bound, 'useful on shared CPU/GPU memory bandwidth platforms'.

dynamic_resolution_scaling.applicability_conditions: Platform allowlist: Xbox One/Series, PS4/PS5 (excluding PSVR), Nintendo Switch, PC (DX12 and Vulkan). Epic states 'Enabling dynamic resolution for platforms that are not on this allowlist is dangerous'.
dynamic_resolution_scaling.limitations: Pixel cost is quadratic: 'The number of pixels drawn by the GPU is actually proportional to Screen Percentage x Screen Percentage.' Known issues: 'Gaussian Depth of Field (DoF) and Distance Field Ambient Occlusion (DFAO) have issues with resolution changes.' There is a frame latency between detection and the resolution change.
dynamic_resolution_scaling.required_data_and_tools: GPU timing feedback, a screen-percentage-driven render-target allocation, and a Stat Unit 'DynRes' readout.

impact.gpu: low to medium (saves GPU by rendering fewer pixels)

dynamic_resolution_scaling.quality_impact: Visible resolution fluctuation; much less objectionable when paired with a good temporal upscaler.
dynamic_resolution_scaling.concept_impact: The standard way to hold a frame-rate target on consoles; effectively mandatory for 60 FPS targets.
dynamic_resolution_scaling.recommended_stage: vertical_slice; needs a defined frame budget before it can be configured.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 3d enable + 2d budget/clamp config + 3d panic-path and upscaler-interference tuning

post_effect_selective.problem: Post-processing cost is a fixed per-pixel tax; applying every effect everywhere at full resolution wastes budget on pixels where the effect is invisible.

implementation_variants.name: Per-effect quality tiers bound to the scalability system
implementation_variants.description: Epic's scalability system exists so that 'Tuning the game's graphics is generally the easiest to scale without affecting gameplay much', and post-process quality is one of the exposed groups.

implementation_variants.name: Half/quarter resolution for the expensive low-frequency effects
implementation_variants.description: 'Half/quarter resolution outputs are used for DoF, Convolution Bloom, Lens Flare, Eye Adaptation, Local Exposure' in UE's PS5/XSX path.

implementation_variants.name: Post-TSR ordering so that effects pay display-resolution cost knowingly
implementation_variants.description: Epic warns of 'Hidden GPU Costs of Temporal Upscaling': 'passes after TSR (motion blur, tonemapper, bloom, etc.) run at display resolution, not render resolution.'

implementation_variants.name: Masked / region-limited application (only where the effect is needed)
implementation_variants.description: The same discipline as VRS and light budgeting: apply the expensive effect only in the region or on the materials that need it.

post_effect_selective.applicability_conditions: Requires the post chain to be modelled as separable passes with individual cost attribution, which render graphs (UE RDG) give you for free via per-pass timing.
post_effect_selective.limitations: Reducing an effect's resolution or coverage can produce visible seams and temporal instability. Ordering matters: an effect placed after the upscaler costs display-resolution pixels.
post_effect_selective.required_data_and_tools: A per-pass GPU timing breakdown, a post-chain visualiser, and screenshot-diff tests to catch quality regressions when tiers change.

impact.gpu: low to medium

post_effect_selective.quality_impact: Low per effect, but the cumulative saving is what funds other features.
post_effect_selective.concept_impact: Lets a project ship a rich look on a wide hardware range.
post_effect_selective.recommended_stage: production; needs final content to judge where cuts are invisible.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 3d per-pass costing + 3d tier mapping + 3d visual regression check

screenspace_light_shafts.problem: Visible god-rays / light shafts that sell atmosphere, without a full volumetric lighting solve.

implementation_variants.name: Radial-blur / occlusion-mask light shafts from the sun's screen position
implementation_variants.description: Classic post-process: build an occlusion mask, then radially blur towards the light's screen-space position. Cheap, but breaks when the light is off-screen or behind the camera.

implementation_variants.name: Reuse the froxel volumetric solve for light shafts
implementation_variants.description: The physically-correct route: light shafts fall out of the volumetric fog solve. Wronski notes the resulting effect is 'very soft and is missing high frequency geometric details, but it fits our art direction and is quite similar to reality (because in the real atmosphere multiple scattering effect takes place and softens the look of light shafts a lot)'.

implementation_variants.name: Half-resolution shafts with temporal jitter
implementation_variants.description: Run the shaft pass at reduced resolution and accumulate - same pattern as other low-frequency effects.

implementation_variants.name: Emissive/analytic card-based shafts (art-authored)
implementation_variants.description: Author the shafts as geometry; zero ray-march cost, full art control, but no automatic response to occluders.

screenspace_light_shafts.applicability_conditions: Screen-space variants need the light on screen and a depth buffer. The volumetric variant needs the whole froxel pipeline. Art-authored variants need art time, not GPU time.
screenspace_light_shafts.limitations: Screen-space shafts flicker when the light crosses the screen edge and cannot account for occluders outside the depth buffer. Volumetric shafts inherit the froxel grid's low resolution and softness.
screenspace_light_shafts.required_data_and_tools: Sun screen position + depth, a mask render target, and a blur/composite pass; or the froxel volumetric pipeline.

impact.gpu: low (post-process variant) to medium (volumetric variant)

screenspace_light_shafts.quality_impact: Medium-high for atmosphere; one of the strongest mood cues per unit cost.
screenspace_light_shafts.concept_impact: Supports an atmospheric art direction cheaply; the volumetric version also unifies with fog and transparency.
screenspace_light_shafts.recommended_stage: vertical_slice; it is part of the look.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 3d mask+blur + 2d temporal stabilisation + 2d art tuning; doubles if the volumetric route is chosen and the pipeline does not exist

relations.note: If volumetrics exist, shafts should come from them rather than from a separate hack.
Shafts are one of the passes to be tiered and down-res'd.

temporal_upscaling.problem: Render at a lower internal resolution and reconstruct a higher-resolution image, buying GPU time with temporal accumulation instead of with pixels.

implementation_variants.name: Unreal Engine Temporal Super Resolution (TSR)
implementation_variants.description: Platform-agnostic temporal upscaler. Epic publishes the only hard numbers I could verify: 'Native 4K: Frame Time: 57.50 ms' vs '1080p upscaled to 4K: Frame Time: 33.37 ms'. TSR's own cost: '~0.79 ms at r.ScreenPercentage=100' and '~0.43 ms at r.ScreenPercentage=50' in the Valley of the Ancient sample. Convergence: 'TSR1spp = 1000 / (ScreenPercentage^2 * FrameRate)', so 50% at 60 Hz needs 66.6 ms.

implementation_variants.name: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 2 (temporal, open source)
implementation_variants.description: Per-dimension scale factors: Quality 1.5x, Balanced 1.7x, Performance 2.0x, Ultra Performance 3.0x. Jitter sequence lengths 18/23/32/72. Requires color + depth + motion vectors at render resolution (jittered), exposure optional. Measured GPU-local memory on RX 6700XT DX12: 4K Quality 448 MB working set (354 persistent + 93 aliasable); 1080p Quality 115 MB.

implementation_variants.name: Intel XeSS Super Resolution
implementation_variants.description: Fixed scale factors in XeSS 1.3+: Ultra Quality 1.5x, Quality 1.7x, Balanced 2.0x, Performance 2.3x, Ultra Performance 3.0x; required mip bias -1 / -1.202 / -1.585 for 2.0x / 2.3x / 3.0x; 'XeSS-SR requires a minimum set of inputs every frame: Jitter, Input color, Dilated high-res motion vectors' (or low-res MV + depth). Runs on any GPU with SM 6.4 / DP4a; D3D11 path is Intel Arc only.

implementation_variants.name: NVIDIA DLSS Super Resolution / DLAA (vendor, Tensor-Core)
implementation_variants.description: 'DLSS Super Resolution boosts performance by using AI to output higher-resolution frames from a lower-resolution input ... samples multiple lower-resolution images and uses motion data and feedback from prior frames'. DLAA is the native-resolution AA mode. Integrated via Streamline, which is 'an open-source cross-IHV solution'.

temporal_upscaling.applicability_conditions: Requires correct per-pixel motion vectors, a jittered projection, and (for best results) an exposure value. TSR runs on 'desktop hardware supporting Shader Model 5 or higher' (D3D11/D3D12/Vulkan/Metal) plus PS5/Xbox Series, and 'TSR's upscaling quality and behavior is strictly identical across all supported platforms'. FSR2 needs D3D12 or Vulkan with HLSL CS_6_2. XeSS needs D3D12/D3D11/Vulkan 1.1.
temporal_upscaling.limitations: All temporal upscalers pay in latency and artefacts. TSR: ghosting on bad motion vectors, translucency problems ('TSR's shading rejection is less forgiving with After DOF translucency'), moire on Nanite at grazing angles, and 'hidden' costs because 'passes after TSR ... run at display resolution, not render resolution'. Nyquist-Shannon history at 200% costs '4x' the history update. Extreme upscaling below 50% 'should only be considered when targeting a display resolution of greater than 4K'.
temporal_upscaling.required_data_and_tools: Jittered projection matrix, motion-vector buffer, depth, exposure, a reactive/responsive mask (FSR2 reactive mask, XeSS responsive pixel mask), and a frame-time/latency measurement tool.

impact.gpu: low (the upscaler itself: measured 0.43-0.79 ms for TSR) but it saves a large fraction of the render pass by lowering its resolution

temporal_upscaling.quality_impact: Can approach native: Epic states rendered frames 'approach the quality of native 4K with input resolutions as low as 1080p'. Degrades to softness and ghosting when motion vectors or jitter are wrong.

temporal_upscaling.recommended_stage: vertical_slice; content (thin geometry, foliage, particles) must be authored with the upscaler's weaknesses in mind.

It delivers up to 4x improvements in frame rate and up to 2x improvements in latency compared to native resolution rendering.'

ml_frame_generation.applicability_conditions: Vendor-hardware-gated (NVIDIA: RTX 40 for FG, RTX 50/Blackwell for MFG; Intel: SM 6.4 capable). Requires a low-latency technology to be integrated alongside (NVIDIA Reflex; Intel XeLL) or the added latency negates the benefit. Requires correct motion vectors / optical flow input and a UI/HUD that is not interpolated incorrectly.
ml_frame_generation.limitations: Frame generation increases displayed frame rate, NOT input responsiveness; the latency claim (up to 2x improvement) is explicitly tied to using Reflex. NVIDIA's multiplier claims (up to 4x, 6x) are vendor marketing figures on NVIDIA's own pages - no independent measurement is available in this pack, and they do not transfer to another game. Generated frames can show artefacts on UI, fast motion and shimmer; the verification method must include slowed-video inspection.
ml_frame_generation.required_data_and_tools: Streamline (NVIDIA) or the XeSS SDK, a latency measurement tool (FrameView / Reflex analyser), an image-comparison tool (ICAT), and slowed-video capture for shimmer.

impact.gpu: medium (generation itself has a real cost; it is not free)

ml_frame_generation.quality_impact: Motion smoothness is genuinely improved; artefact risk is on UI, particles and fast transients.

ml_frame_generation.recommended_stage: late_production_or_post_launch as an optional mode; it is a platform-specific feature, not a core system.

lightmap_2d_baking.problem: Per-pixel 2D lighting (normal-mapped sprites, many point lights, soft shadows) costs fill rate and draw setup on every frame. implementation_variants.name: Baked lightmap overlay texture (multiply/additive layer over the tilemap)
implementation_variants.description: Pre-compute irradiance for the static scene into a texture atlas, then composite it over the background as a single textured quad (multiply for shadows, additive for glows). Cost per frame becomes one full-screen blend instead of N light passes.

implementation_variants.name: Additive sprite 'fake lights' instead of real 2D lights
implementation_variants.description: Godot documents this directly: a section titled 'Using additive sprites as a faster alternative to 2D lights'. The light is a pre-authored gradient sprite, so there is no per-light shader work and no shadow-caster geometry at all.

implementation_variants.name: Per-sprite / per-vertex baked tint
implementation_variants.description: Bake the light contribution into vertex colours or into a per-instance tint so it costs nothing in the fragment shader. Cheapest option; only supports very low-frequency lighting.

implementation_variants.name: Hybrid: bake the ambient/static term, keep 1-2 dynamic lights
implementation_variants.description: Bake indirect and static emitters, leave a small budget of real dynamic lights for the player and moving objects. Godot's 2D light documentation exposes Max Distance and shadow filter quality (PCF5 vs PCF13) as the knobs for what remains dynamic.

lightmap_2d_baking.applicability_conditions: Only worth it when the 2D lighting is dominated by static emitters and the camera moves (so per-frame relighting is repeated). Projects with fully dynamic time-of-day or destructible lighting cannot bake.
lightmap_2d_baking.limitations: Baked data cannot react to gameplay without re-baking or blending; it costs texture memory and build time; and it interacts badly with parallax/scrolling layers unless the bake is done in the same space as the composite.
lightmap_2d_baking.required_data_and_tools: A bake tool that can rasterise occluders into a light space (Godot's LightOccluder2D / SDF collision shape is the documented equivalent), an atlas packer, and a composite pass in the 2D renderer.

impact.gpu: low to medium reduction in 2D lighting fill cost; no published measurement available for this pass
impact.vram: medium (one or more full-screen-resolution baked textures per scene)

lightmap_2d_baking.quality_impact: Baked 2D lighting is smoother and cheaper to author but static; moving characters will not cast light onto the baked layer unless a dynamic overlay is added.
lightmap_2d_baking.concept_impact: Enables dense, art-directed 2D lighting on low-end and mobile hardware where per-pixel 2D lights are unaffordable.
lightmap_2d_baking.recommended_stage: prototype, before the 2D art pipeline is locked; retro-fitting a bake step means re-authoring level lighting.

effort_person_days.formula: p50 = 5d bake tool + 3d composite pass + 4d re-authoring and tuning of one reference level; p80 = round(1.6 * p50). No published measurement; expert_estimate.

relations.note: Same idea in 3D: precompute static irradiance into an atlas. The 2D case is much simpler because there is no UV-unwrap problem.
Whatever is not baked still needs a per-light budget; Godot exposes Max Distance and PCF5/PCF13 for that.
The hybrid variant is exactly a priority budget: baked = free, dynamic = limited count.

lightmap_2d_baking.verification: Compare frame time before and after baking on a reference level, at the maximum dynamic-light count, and confirm the visual delta is accepted by art.

claims.locator: Section: 'Using additive sprites as a faster alternative to 2D lights'

claims.locator: Sections: 'Common light properties', 'Setting up shadows'
